transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Start time: 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Omar (Redwood CSM), Priya (CTO), Luis (ML Eng), Ellen (Data Eng), Marcus (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Arbor is evaluating Redwood for a retrieval+rerank architecture. Primary concerns: sustained throughput for 500-2k QPS on short queries, embedding dims (512 vs 1024), hybrid search with vector DB (they use self-hosted Milvus today), where to host (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved nodes vs Private VPC) given compliance and latency SLOs. They want a POC comparing Redwood Hosted + Pinecone style vdb fallback vs Redwood Dedicated serving embeddings + in-house vdb, and a clear cost/latency decision matrix.

Topics:
- Current stack and constraints
- Endpoint latency SLOs and tail latency
- Embedding dimension, quantization, ops per second
- Hybrid search + rerank integration patterns
- Private deployment constraints (VPC/KMS/audit logs)
- Next steps and POC scoping

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, AE at Redwood. Quick intros real fast please.
[00:10] Priya Desai: Hi I'm Priya, CTO at Arbor Analytics. We're evaluating options for a relevance pipeline that can scale to low-latency recommendations and search.
[00:18] Luis Romero: Luis here, ML Eng, I run the embed pipeline and rerank models.
[00:22] Ellen Park: Ellen, data infra engineer, I manage our Milvus clusters and ETL.
[00:27] Marcus Cole: Marcus, Head of Product, I'm here for product/OKR alignment.
[00:31] Jenna Liu: Jenna from Redwood, Solutions Eng, I'll cover architecture and POC specifics.
[00:36] Samir Patel: Cool. High level, we want to understand your workloads and success criteria. Priya, what's the hard requirement?
[00:45] Priya Desai: Hard requirements are basically: sub-100ms p50 for top-k retrieval + rerank within a 200ms budget for end-to-end for our primary use-case. For enterprise customers we need SOC2-ish audit logs and SSO, and some datasets must remain in our VPC or approved region. Cost target is also strict — we want predictable unit cost not crazy overage spikes.
[01:10] Samir Patel: Makes sense. Can you share current numbers? QPS, embed dims, latency?
[01:15] Luis Romero: Right now our production is Milvus self-hosted on GCP. We push 700 QPS steady during peak, spikes to 2k for promotions. Embeddings are 1024 dims from a finetuned open model. Retrieval p95 is 120ms on Milvus but end-to-end p95 with rerank is 380ms, so we need to cut the rerank overhead.
[01:40] Ellen Park: Also our infra ops cost is growing, so there's interest in offloading serving. But we cannot send PII to a public API for some clients; they'd need private deployment or VPC.
[01:52] Jenna Liu: Thanks. A few axes we typically look at: embedding dimension (512 vs 1024), quantized embeddings, where to run the rerank (co-located with vdb vs separate inference cluster), and caching/prefix-KV for hot queries to reduce cost.
[02:10] Marcus Cole: The team ran a small A/B — lower-dim embeddings at 512 shaved latency but lost recall on specific product searches. Curious how Redwood handles hybrid search — we sometimes do sparse + dense.
[02:25] Samir Patel: Quick product note: Redwood has three deployment modes — Hosted API for easiest onboarding, Dedicated reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput, and Private VPC/on-prem for data-sensitive workloads. We can also route by policy for cost/latency.
[02:43] Priya Desai: For the Private option, is the control plane still with Redwood? We need to be able to rotate keys and have audit logs in our SIEM.
[02:51] Jenna Liu: For Private, the control plane can be customer-managed with optional on-prem packages. KMS integrations and audit log forwarding to your SIEM are supported — we'll share the security docs.
[03:05] Luis Romero: Could you describe how rerank is best positioned? We currently do a top-100 candidate rerank with a cross-encoder on a GPU pod; that's the expensive bit.
[03:16] Jenna Liu: Right, common patterns: 1) Redwood serves embeddings and returns top-K vectors to your vdb, then your rerank runs separately; 2) Redwood runs retrieval and rerank in a combined flow (we can host a rerank model in the same Dedicated pool to avoid transfer latency and use continuous batching); 3) hybrid approach: do a coarse retrieval in vdb then call Redwood for rerank only on the reduced set.
[03:44] Samir Patel: For throughput, if you want to hit sustained 1k QPS with rerank, Dedicated pools usually make sense because they let you reserve GPUs and control batching/parallelism. Hosted can work for bursty workloads but cost and tail latency are less predictable at high sustained QPS.
[04:03] Luis Romero: That resonates. Our pattern is sustained with spikes. Can you give ballpark numbers: two approaches 512 vs 1024 dims, what is the token or vector time difference?
[04:17] Jenna Liu: Ballpark: 512-dim embeddings reduce memory and similarity compute by roughly 2x vs 1024, so throughput for cosine similarity on same hardware almost doubles. Rerank cost depends on model size — a small cross-encoder (distil-size) can do many hundreds of QPS per GPU with batching; a large cross-encoder is tens of QPS. We can share benchmark spreadsheet showing ops/sec per model shape.
[04:45] Priya Desai: What about quantized embeddings in storage to Milvus — any caveats? We've thought of 8-bit/4-bit storage to save vector DB costs.
[04:54] Jenna Liu: Quantized embeddings are great for storage and network, but you might lose some retrieval fidelity, especially on fine-grained product similarity. We recommend running a precision sweep (512/1024 x FP32/INT8/INT4) on a representative query set to see recall delta. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization points based on your eval set.
[05:15] Ellen Park: On the vector DB side, we use HNSW in Milvus. If we offload retrieval to Redwood, do we still need Milvus?
[05:24] Samir Patel: You might, depending on migration/multi-tenant needs. Two patterns: use Redwood as a serving layer for embeddings and retrieval (we have fast approximate nearest neighbor implementations) or keep Milvus for storage and indexing and use Redwood as the rerank+inference layer with a tight integration (point-in-time consistency, bulk upserts). For gradual migration, many customers keep their vdb and integrate via an adapter.
[05:46] Luis Romero: How do you handle cache/kv for very hot queries? We have very skewed distributions.
[05:51] Jenna Liu: We support prefix caching and hot-query caching. For hot queries we can store results in Redis or use our in-run KV cache to avoid repeated heavy rerank calls. Policy-driven TTLs and invalidation hooks are supported.
[06:05] Marcus Cole: We also have regulatory clients in EU where data residency matters. Does Redwood Hosted offer region locking?
[06:12] Samir Patel: Hosted regions exist (NA/EU/APAC), but for strict residency and control, Private VPC or Dedicated in a chosen region is the recommended path. We'll share our region table and compliance docs.
[06:25] Priya Desai: Let's talk POC. We want to evaluate: (A) Redwood Hosted retrieval + our Milvus rerank hybrid, (B) Redwood Dedicated with embedding serving + rerank co-located, and (C) Private VPC with our security controls. The evaluation matrix needs to measure cost, p50/p95 latency, and recall at top-10.
[06:47] Jenna Liu: Perfect. For (A) we can run a smoke test with a small sample and show integration latency. For (B) we can provision a small Dedicated pool and run your 10k-doc sample with 512/1024 sweeps and quantization. For (C) we'll sketch what Private deployment looks like and the lead time for infra.
[07:06] Luis Romero: Lead times are important. How long to stand up Dedicated vs Private?
[07:10] Samir Patel: Dedicated can be spun up in days to a couple weeks depending on quota; Private VPC/on-prem can be 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS integration. We will confirm exact timelines once we scope infra.
[07:25] Priya Desai: Security checklist: SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2. We also need data flow diagrams for PII flows.
[07:34] Jenna Liu: We'll send the security pack and a draft data flow diagram. We'll also include options for customer-managed keys.
[07:45] Ellen Park: Question — if we move rerank to Redwood Dedicated, what's the data residency model for embeddings? Are embeddings stored in Redwood?
[07:53] Jenna Liu: By default Hosted stores embeddings transiently for caching; for Dedicated we can configure storage policies — options include no-persistence (in-memory), encrypted persistent store in your cloud account, or forwarding to your existing vdb. We'll capture your preference in the POC plan.
[08:12] Marcus Cole: Pricing model: we need predictable committed pricing for Dedicated but an option to burst. Can we get a committed rate for baseline and a burst tier?
[08:20] Samir Patel: Yes. Dedicated is reserved capacity with commits; burst options exist for short-lived scale. We'll put an example pricing table in the follow-up.
[08:30] Priya Desai: Metrics to report during POC: p50/p95 retrieval, end-to-end rerank p50/p95, cost per 1M queries, recall@10 and latency tail distribution. Also operational metrics like error rates, infra alerts.
[08:45] Jenna Liu: Understood. We'll instrument the POC with tracing to break down time across retrieval, network, rerank, and batching overhead.
[08:56] Ellen Park: Small nit — our current Milvus uses HNSW efSearch params tuned. Will Redwood support similar indexing knobs?
[09:03] Jenna Liu: We expose ANN tuning parameters and will work with your ops team to match efSearch/efConstruction-like parameters or map them to our approximate NN config.
[09:15] Luis Romero: On the ML side, I'd like to try reducing dims to 512 with an intermediate fine-tune and see recall impact. If we move rerank to Redwood, can you host our rerank model (weights) securely?
[09:27] Jenna Liu: Yes — we support hosting customer models in Dedicated or Private. For Hosted, there are tighter controls and some customers prefer Private for model custody. We can provide an execution isolation write-up.
[09:40] Samir Patel: Let's capture immediate risks: 1) recall drop with lower dims/quantization; 2) private deployment lead time; 3) cost predictability for Hosted under sustained QPS.
[09:53] Priya Desai: Agreed. Also data egress if we use Hosted — that could add cost and compliance issues.
[10:00] Samir Patel: We'll compare the egress implications in the cost model. Jenna, anything else on architecture?
[10:05] Jenna Liu: One more: for hybrid search we recommend a two-stage flow — coarse recall from vdb (top 500), light embedding pruning on the host to top 100, then cross-encoder rerank. This minimizes GPU usage for rerank. We'll sketch a sample diagram.
[10:25] Marcus Cole: That sounds like the approach we used conceptually. For the POC, can we set target thresholds: p50 end-to-end < 100ms for the 512-dim config, p95 under 200ms, recall@10 within 3% of baseline?
[10:37] Priya Desai: Yes those thresholds are acceptable for the POC. If the 512 path fails recall, we'll evaluate cost tradeoffs.
[10:45] Samir Patel: Great. Operational questions — do you have SRE access to logs and traces during POC?
[10:50] Ellen Park: We'll need read-only logs and the ability to integrate with our PagerDuty.
[10:55] Jenna Liu: We'll enable log forwarding and read-only dashboards. For PagerDuty we can set-up webhooks.
[11:02] Luis Romero: A few micro questions: do you support on-the-fly reranking of cached vectors, and can we warm caches?
[11:10] Jenna Liu: Yes to both. We support warming strategies and can re-rank cached results with a low-latency path.
[11:18] Priya Desai: Any red flags on model format? We mostly use ONNX for retrieval models and PyTorch for rerank.
[11:24] Jenna Liu: We accept ONNX and PyTorch; for Dedicated we can run PyTorch native or ONNX depending on optimization. We'll note that large cross-encoders benefit from compilation/quantization.
[11:34] Samir Patel: Ok wrapping up — action items and next steps. We'll send the benchmark spreadsheet, security docs, and a proposed POC calendar. POC kickoff target week of 9/22.
[11:45] Priya Desai: Sounds good. Ellen will share a 10k doc sample and two query lists (promotions and organic).
[11:52] Ellen Park: Yep we'll share by Monday.
[11:55] Marcus Cole: We'll also share product acceptance criteria for the POC.
[11:58] Samir Patel: Excellent. Thanks all. Jenna will follow up on the POC plan.
[12:05] Jenna Liu: I'll send the draft and bench spreadsheet.
[12:10] End of recording.
